scope: Anonymous, read-only assessment of current public guidance for the approved HyP3 Basic RTC route. No account, token, job, product, pixel, or external-custody access occurred.

public_sources.finding: ASF says anyone with Earthdata Login credentials may use HyP3 Basic to request On Demand products without payment, with a monthly free-credit allotment and 14-day output retention. This is Basic service guidance, not the private accepted agreement or a generated-product license.

ASF distinguishes Basic from HyP3+ and says submitted jobs, user IDs, metadata, and resulting downloads are publicly visible. The owner previously accepted public visibility; no job has been submitted.
ASF asks users of On Demand products to retain the product-specific acknowledgement and relevant DOIs in each multi-file product README. The exact future README has not been obtained.
The posted CC0 product clause expressly concerns HyP3+; it cannot be assigned to HyP3 Basic outputs by inference. The route uses Basic only and authorizes no paid credits.

The European Commission permits lawful Sentinel data reproduction, distribution, adaptation, and combination with source notices. This governs underlying Copernicus Sentinel data; it does not by itself establish the license of ASF's processed RTC package or its ancillary DEM.
ASF says new users are prompted to accept its End-User License Agreement, but this public page does not give the exact agreement text or version accepted by the owner.

The current Basic POST /jobs schema advertises HTTP 200 and an explicit validate_only boolean. The approved request supplies every current RTC_GAMMA option, avoiding unstated defaults in the validation response identity check.

Recent public source preserves supplied job parameters while adding defaults, and performs credit decrement and database writes only when dry_run is false. This is source-code evidence, not proof of the deployed service's behavior.

next_dependency: Await the one owner-run validate-only result. Any processing-job gate must separately reconcile the proposal's exact-terms condition and current Basic product local-use rights; a future product's README must be inspected before product-specific acknowledgement or publication claims.
claim_boundary: Public documentation establishes a plausible Basic service path and the underlying Sentinel legal notice, not the owner's exact ASF agreement, deployed no-charge dry-run behavior, a processed-package license, live scene eligibility, a product QA pass, or a scientific map.
